top_signal.title: My story of how I built a business with 30+ staff over 10 years. Today we officially closed down with $0 in debt. Looking for advice.
top_signal.summary: My business failed and I wanted figure out what to do next. Need your help figuring things out now on how to go forward. I was consulting and doing marketing gigs, but now my customers aren't making money, and others are using tech to lower costs.   So it's difficult. because I watched the business of over thirty people working under me shrink down to just under five in the span of 2 years. And there was just no hope in keeping it open. It's time to figure out what to do next, because I'm at the crossroads again, and this is not anything new for a business owner but I'm at a different point of my life right now as I'm closer to the age of fifty and farther from forty.   And now it's really interesting because there's a lot more to lose than to gain, and things are kind of coming into perspective. Whereas before I could take very big risks and not even worry about failing. But I think that midlife crisis thing is a real thing because it makes me think about what am I headed into? Cause I'm at this crossroad where I don't have a pension lined up for me. As a solopreneur running businesses I take risks and reap the rewards, but also learn from the failures and own them too. And so I've been doing that for my whole life. Nothing new here, it's just that my latest gig which lasted just over ten years has now come to an end and now Im ten years older.
